paper.title: Learning to Build the Environment: Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis
paper.central_claim: EvoEnv co-trains a shared generator/solver policy to synthesize, validate, freeze and reuse executable reasoning environments, preserving stable reward while an evolving curriculum improves external reasoning performance without external problem-answer training data.
paper.scope_reason: The retained, evaluated non-weight object is an executable sampler/renderer/scorer environment pool, not merely a weight recipe or disposable synthetic answers. Admission, pool growth, oracle audit and curriculum controls evaluate that harness object. Weight RL is essential to the improver and solver; frozen A3 permits this mixed case but does not convert solver-weight transfer into retained-harness transfer.

evidence.quote: A reward source that is policy-coupled, learned, or per-instance can still drive useful curricula, but it does not by itself give a durable, sample-many object that can be calibrated and reused.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors identify the fixed/moving reward-source distinction and claim environment-level reuse rather than one-off questions. This is their positioning, not independently checked priority.

evidence.quote: Reference answers are computed by deterministic Python execution and reach the scorer through the code path; the solver sees only the rendered natural-language prompt.
evidence.support_explanation: The solver's information boundary and frozen executable oracle are explicit. Executability and determinism alone do not certify semantic correctness of model-written code.

evidence.quote: Scorer contract: reference answers score positively; perturbations, malformed answers, and type mismatches do not; parser does not leak hidden references.
evidence.support_explanation: A concrete mechanical admission contract exists beyond raw solver difficulty. It tests internal consistency and leakage but can miss a mutually consistent wrong prompt/oracle.

evidence.quote: accumulates 840 accepted environments within 100 steps, while the tag-prototype count reaches 45.
evidence.support_explanation: Non-weight code artifacts are actually retained and audited during the run. Tag diversity is not itself downstream utility or semantic certification.

evidence.quote: We isolate the contribution of the two generator-reward components: quality reward (validation and difficulty shaping) and diversity reward (novelty-gated exploration bonus). Each ablation removes one component while keeping training steps, seeds, and evaluation protocol identical to the full
evidence.support_explanation: Reward-component ablations hold important factors fixed, but quality bundles validation and difficulty. Neither an independent semantic-gate removal nor a frozen generated-pool reuse comparison is reported.

evidence.quote: trains only on self-generated executable environments from ten seeds, without using problem-answer data from the evaluation benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: External benchmark separation is stated. It concerns solver-weight training/evaluation; contamination tests and a frozen retained-environment transfer study are not supplied.

evidence.quote: The reviewer reliably catches greedy-for-optimal substitutions, hardcoded or trivially-derivable reference answers, mathematical-property violations (e.g., a non-prime claimed prime), and most incorrect-recurrence bugs that surface on a small traced instance.

evidence.quote: The reviewer therefore only needs to be biased correctly relative to the external reference, not to match it perfectly.

Table 5 deployed tuple (30,5,40,4) implies 34 buggy/45 correct, inconsistent with the setup and caption's 35/44; reported 88.2% recall agrees with 30/34, not 30/35. These are measurement caveats, not invented missing materials.

evidence.quote: A reasoning environment is a reusable executable artifact with four routines: a sampler that generates latent task instances, an oracle that computes reference answers, a renderer that turns instances into natural-language prompts, and a scorer that evaluates solver responses.

evidence.quote: Candidate environments enter the pool only when they satisfy four contracts: they execute under a strict interface; their oracle and scorer match the advertised task under conservative semantic self-review; sampled instances are hard-but-solvable for the current policy; and the pool remains broad enough to avoid template collapse.
evidence.support_explanation: 准入规则：四条合约(执行/语义自审/难度/新颖)。

signatures.object: Reusable Python environment pool containing sampler, hidden reference, prompt renderer, parser and scorer
signatures.information: Generator sees seed/environment code; semantic reviewer sees code, sampled prompts, hidden/reference states and probes; solver sees rendered prompt only. Frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeds prompt template and cleaned generation body.
signatures.operation: Generate VerifiableEnvironment code; validate L1 interface, L2 execution, L3 determinism, L4 variation and L5 scorer contract; run three same-policy semantic reviews with any-reject; estimate current solver pass rate on eight fresh instances; admit nontrivial/nonzero, semantically approved, sufficiently novel code.
signatures.output: Frozen executable environment reused for many sampled instances and future generator context
signatures.conditions: Compact deterministic, cheaply executable algorithmic tasks; parser/reference separation and semantic validity. Tests do not establish all-input correctness.
signatures.feedback: Mechanical validation layer, measured solver pass rate, prompt/code embedding novelty, semantic veto
signatures.selection_rule: L5 plus semantic approval plus 0<estimated pass rate<1 plus similarity below0.80. Calibration is one solver answer per fresh instance, up to8. Novelty compares prompt/code similarity with mixture0.5.
signatures.selection_data: Current candidate probes, sampled solver rollouts and active/seed environment pool; no external benchmark failures stated as generation input.
signatures.persistence: Accepted code remains frozen in active pool; rotate every10 steps after maximum5 epochs; retired items may remain generator seeds; original-seed floor0.2. Explicit per-version regression rollback not described.
signatures.later_use: Sample new prompts and deterministic rewards for later solver groups; accepted environments can condition subsequent environment generation.
signatures.claimed_effect: Stable reusable reward with continuing curriculum expansion,840 accepted environments and45 tag prototypes at100 steps.
signatures.failure_boundary: Prompt/oracle can agree yet be wrong; same-policy semantic veto and m=8 calibration do not prove correctness. Deterministic Python domain only.

signatures.object: Shared role-conditioned generator/solver weights controlling construction and use of the environment pool
signatures.information: Generator gets mechanically computed quality/difficulty plus novelty; semantic review affects admission but never scalar generator reward; solver receives frozen-code scores.
signatures.operation: Compute frontier reward near pass-rate0.3, vary novelty pressure from similarity EMA, normalize advantages separately for generator and solver groups, optimize joint GRPO with generator scale0.3 and KL reference, then regenerate against updated solver.
signatures.output: Updated role-shared policy plus incrementally replaced non-weight curriculum
signatures.conditions: Starting policy can write valid code and solve some accepted tasks; shared-role optimization must not drift into uninformative tasks.
signatures.feedback: Executable scorer rewards solver and mechanically validated frontier/novelty rewards generator; semantic veto is not trained as a numerical self-reward.
signatures.selection_rule: Generator updates can include semantically rejected but mechanically valid candidates; only admitted environments supply solver rewards. No post-update held-out promotion gate is described.
signatures.selection_data: Self-generated environments, current solver calibrations and ten fixed seeds, four adapted from Luogu
signatures.persistence: Weights and admitted code pool carry forward through100 training steps; evaluator code stays fixed per admitted artifact even while policy changes.
signatures.later_use: Updated policy generates new environments and solves freshly sampled instances; final solver weights evaluated on external benchmarks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Mean benchmark pass@1 improves49.2→53.1,72.4→74.8,71.0→73.2 across three backbones.
signatures.failure_boundary: External tests measure solver weights, not transport of a frozen evolved pool to another solver; no independent improved-proposer versus old-proposer descendant test.

gap.author_gap: Fixed RLVR environments saturate; policy-coupled self-labeling drifts, while per-instance executable tasks are consumed once and do not create a durable, reusable reward-generating environment.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete change of unit from problem to executable sampler/renderer/scorer is reconstructable. Authors name RLVE, R-Zero and AZR/SPC/SCA families; static RLVE and R-Zero are tested. Claims about prior methods' lack of reusable objects remain author-supplied positioning because original neighbours are absent.

gap.residue: A stable oracle need not require a static curriculum: keep each accepted scorer frozen while generating and rotating the environment population.
gap.stakes: Manual curriculum coverage and self-generated reward drift constrain reasoning RL; this paper addresses compact deterministic algorithmic environments, not general world grounding.
gap.method_response: Validate executable objects before reuse, calibrate frontier and novelty, and separate semantic admission from generator scalar reward while co-training roles.
gap.remaining_gap: Semantic correctness still depends partly on same-policy review; no matched frozen generated pool or direct fresh-solver portability test, no demonstrated indefinitely sustained evolution or full actual loop costs.
unresolved: Request pinned original RLVE, R-Zero, AZR/SPC/SCA and nearest reusable-environment synthesis papers for both seats through a re-fixed shared package; do not infer verified novelty from the authors' comparison table.

claims.text: Evolving executable environments improve external reasoning for three model families without external problem-answer training data.
claims.setting: 100 training steps; Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Qwen3-4B-Thinking and Nemotron-Cascade-8B; eight math/science/code benchmarks.
claims.baseline/control: Untrained policy, R-Zero, DAPO-Math-17k with stated compute matching and fixed RLVE with step matching.
claims.selection_vs_test: Generation uses ten seeds and current solver calibration, not external benchmark problems as stated; held-out evaluation tests final solver weights, not reuse of a frozen harness with a fresh solver.
claims.result/denominator: Mean pass@1 across eight benchmarks49.2→53.1,72.4→74.8,71.0→73.2. Five math benchmark evaluations averaged over16 sampling runs; AMC23/GPQA/LCB single-run. Three backbones are not independent training seeds.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported external solver-weight improvements under disclosed seed use; no unlimited evolution or directly isolated retained-pool transfer claim.

claims.text: Quality/difficulty and novelty rewards jointly sustain a useful expanding curriculum.
claims.setting: Qwen3-4B-Thinking reward ablation; Qwen3-4B-Instruct100-step pool audit and held-out dynamics.
claims.baseline/control: w/o Quality, w/o Diversity; fixed-environment RLVR.
claims.selection_vs_test: External metrics test solver outcomes; pool count, tags and admission rates are in-loop diagnostics.
claims.result/denominator: Table2 seven-benchmark mean gain+2.4 full versus+0.5 without quality and+0.6 without diversity. Pool840 accepted environments/45 tag prototypes at100 steps;50 unseen RLVE environments72.4→80.4 versus fixed near72%.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Component rewards help this training recipe and generated pool expands; tag separation is not a lower-bound proof of semantic families, and comparison does not isolate reusable objects from all other synthesis choices.

claims.text: Frozen code validation and same-policy semantic review provide sufficiently stable reward without a stronger teacher in training.
claims.setting: 79 earlier-run environments already passing mechanical L1-L5; deployed3-review any-reject gate compared to single GPT-5.4 review.
claims.baseline/control: Single review, majority3, all-reject3 and trivial label predictors.
claims.selection_vs_test: Offline external-model audit on earlier candidates, not independent theorem/exhaustive oracle certification; audit is not the generator scalar reward.
